7. The abdomen appears distended.
8. Watery eyes and excessive salivation are observed.
9. In adult animals, reproductive organs become flaccid due to inadequate nutrition [પોષણ].
10. Skin diseases may develop.

# 6. Signs and Identification of Estrus/Heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] in Animals
When cows and buffaloes come into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]/estrus, the following external and internal changes are observed.
## External Signs
- The cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] shows a desire to mate with a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો].
- Becomes restless, frequently raises its tail, looks back repeatedly, and sniffs other animals.
- The cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] becomes agitated, runs around, bellows, or exhibits mounting [એકબીજા પર ચઢવું] behavior.
- Mounts other animals or stands still to allow mounting [એકબીજા પર ચઢવું].
- Swelling appears on the vulvar lips.
- A transparent, viscous fluid (mucus) is discharged from the vulva.
- The animal [પશુ] urinates frequently in small amounts.
- If the animal [પશુ] in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is lactating, milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ] may drop or fluctuate.
## Internal Signs
- Blood circulation and muscle contractions in the reproductive organs of the cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] increase.
- Due to the effect of estrogen, the cervix, vagina, and uterine glands produce mucus.
- The uterine body [બૈડા/બરડા]/horns [શિંગડા] become elevated, firm, and curved like a ram’s horns [શિંગડા].
- The cervix opens.
- A mature follicle [બીજમસો] (Graafian follicle [બીજમસો]) can be palpated on the ovary.
- The previous corpus luteum regresses and appears smaller, leading to a significant decrease in progesterone secretion in blood and milk.
- Careful observation of each animal [પશુ] 3–4 times a day can help identify at least some of the above signs.

- If necessary, confirmation can be obtained by rectal palpation [હાથથી દબાવીને તપાસવું] by staff at the artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] center, and timely insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] should be carried out.

# **Silent Heat [શાંત વેતર] (Subestrus) in Buffaloes and Its Management**
**Dr. Nishchay K. Patel, Dr. Ditesh J. Savani, and Dr. Mehtul D. Patel**

Buffaloes constitute a significant livestock [પશુઓ] population in India. Out of the total milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in the country, 56% comes from buffaloes, making them crucial for milk procurement. Buffalo [ભેંસ] milk is highly popular due to its higher fat [ફેટ] content and creamy white color. Due to these unique characteristics, buffalo [ભેંસ] milk is preferred over cow [ગાય] milk in various dairy products. In Gujarat, buffaloes primarily belong to **four breeds**: **Mehsani, Surti, Jafarabadi, and Jari**, which are commonly found across the state based on regional availability.

During the summer season, **silent heat [શાંત વેતર] (subestrus)** is a major issue in buffaloes. Farmers often face difficulties in detecting whether their buffaloes are in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]. ## Question-6: How to inseminate a cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] after calving [વિયાણ]?

**Answer:** After calving [વિયાણ], if a cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] comes into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] within the first two months (60 days), insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] should not be done. After this period, insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (natural or artificial) should be performed during the first heat cycle [તાણ/ગરમી]. During the post-calving [વિયાણ પછી] period, the uterus [ગર્ભાશય] becomes enlarged, so it takes time to return to its normal condition. Additionally, if there is any infection [ચેપ] or abnormality in the uterus [ગર્ભાશય], it resolves on its own.
## Question-7: What are the rules of the artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (AI) method?

**Answer:** In the artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] method, semen from high-quality bulls/buffalo [ભેંસ] bulls with superior milk-yielding genetic traits is used. This results in calves (heifers/young bulls) with high genetic merit and increased milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in the inseminated cows/buffaloes. If a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો]/buffalo [ભેંસ] used for natural mating [કુદરતી ફળવણી] carries diseases like brucellosis [ચેપી ગર્ભપાત (બ્રુસેલોસીસ)], it can spread to cows/buffaloes, but this risk is eliminated with AI. A single bull [સાંઢ/આખલો]/buffalo [ભેંસ] can naturally mate with around 100 cows/buffaloes per year, whereas with AI, 2,000 to 3,000 cows/buffaloes can be inseminated in a year.
## Question-8: What diseases may occur in animals after calving [વિયાણ]?

**Answer:** After calving [વિયાણ], animals may suffer from conditions such as retained placenta [માટી ન ખસવી], metritis [ગર્ભાશયની દીવાલ નો સોજો], mastitis [આઉનો/બાવલાનો સોજો], fever [તાવ] (milk fever [સૂવાનો રોગ (મિલ્ક ફીવર)/દૂધીઓ તાવ]), dystocia [વિયાણમાં મુશ્કેલી], uterine prolapse [ગર્ભાશય બહાર નીકળી જવું/દિલ ધસી આવવું/વાખર (વાખોર ) નિકળવી], and other diseases.
## Question-9: How is the placenta [મેલી/જર] expelled after calving [વિયાણ]?

**Answer:** The placenta [મેલી/જર] (afterbirth) is normally expelled at the time of birth. In many cases, it is expelled within 8–10 hours. If it remains retained for a longer period, it can lead to infections, so veterinary care should be sought.

# Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

This is a scientific method in which semen from a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] is collected artificially, tested in a laboratory, and then deposited into the reproductive tract of a female in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] using scientific instruments.
## Why Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]?
- For rapid improvement of livestock [પશુઓ] breeds
- To achieve higher milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in less time
- For extensive use of semen from proven high-quality bulls
## Laws of Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

- Naturally, a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or buffalo [ભેંસ] can impregnate about 100 females in a year. Through artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], more than 2000 females can be impregnated in a year. Thus, the use of high-quality bulls or buffaloes accelerates breed improvement.
- Fewer bulls or buffaloes are required, allowing for the selection of the best males.
- When cows or buffaloes are naturally impregnated, diseased males can spread diseases to many females. In artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], the risk of disease transmission is eliminated.
- During insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], the female's reproductive organs are examined, allowing for the treatment of any defects.

- When a female is in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], the livestock [પશુઓ] owner does not need to search for a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or buffalo [ભેંસ]. A trained insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] technician can perform the insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] on time using semen from high-quality males.
- Records of insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] dates facilitate accurate pregnancy [ગર્ભ] testing and planning.
- Semen from high-quality bulls or buffaloes stored in semen centers can be used even after their death.
- Semen from high-quality livestock [પશુઓ] can be transported to any location, making good quality semen available in villages at minimal cost.
- Facilitates crossbreeding [સંકરણ].
- Simplifies the impregnation process and increases the conception rate [ગર્ભાધાન દર].

### 4. Uterine Prolapse [ગર્ભાશય બહાર નીકળી જવું/દિલ ધસી આવવું/વાખર (વાખોર ) નિકળવી] (Prolapse [દેહ બતાવવી/આર બતાવવું (ગર્ભાશય બહાર આવવું)] of the Uterus [ગર્ભાશય])

In cattle [પશુ], before or after parturition, the vagina and part of the uterus [ગર્ભાશય] may prolapse [દેહ બતાવવી/આર બતાવવું (ગર્ભાશય બહાર આવવું)] through the vulva. This condition is locally referred to as *Mati Bhasi Javi* (soil-stained), *Deel Niknavu*, or *Yoni Lānsh* (vaginal prolapse [દેહ બતાવવી/આર બતાવવું (ગર્ભાશય બહાર આવવું)]).
**Causes**:
- During pregnancy [ગર્ભ], especially in the last trimester, the placenta [મેલી/જર] secretes excess estrogen, which relaxes the uterine ligaments.
- The vulva becomes flaccid, and increased pressure on the organs may cause prolapse [દેહ બતાવવી/આર બતાવવું (ગર્ભાશય બહાર આવવું)].

- Occurs due to low calcium [કેલ્શિયમ] levels in the blood; there is actually no fever [તાવ]. May also cause dystocia [વિયાણમાં મુશ્કેલી], retained placenta [માટી ન ખસવી] (ROP), and uterine prolapse [ગર્ભાશય બહાર નીકળી જવું/દિલ ધસી આવવું/વાખર (વાખોર ) નિકળવી].
- Typically occurs within 72 hours of calving [વિયાણ]. The initial stage involves excitability with fine tremors over the flank and loins, ear twitching, and head bobbing.
- Complete milking [પૂરેપૂરું દોહન] during the first 48 hours after calving [વિયાણ] may precipitate milk fever [સૂવાનો રોગ (મિલ્ક ફીવર)/દૂધીઓ તાવ] in some cases.
- The animal [પશુ] is unable to stand and, in later stages, becomes recumbent, first with its neck [ગળું] turned to one side and then laterally. The eye reflex is also lost.
- In the final stage, the animal [પશુ] becomes unconscious with a subnormal temperature.

- Hypocalcemia [કેલ્શિયમની ઉણપ] also exists in a subclinical form, with a greater risk of animals developing fever [તાવ], metritis [ગર્ભાશયની દીવાલ નો સોજો], and ketosis [કિટોસીસ/ઊર્જાની કમીથી થતો રોગ]. More losses are thought to occur from this form.

### Definition

Biosecurity in bovine farms refers to the management practices that reduce the chances of disease-causing agents from entering, spreading, or leaving the premises where bovines are maintained. Additionally, certain diseases are zoonotic, so effective biosecurity also reduces risks to human health.

# A. HEAT [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]
- Heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is a period in which female animal [પશુ] shows interest in other animals.

- Generally adult heifer [પાડી]/cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] comes in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] after every 21 days but may come in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] any time between 18/24 days.
- This period may last from 6 to 30 hours.
- To maximize productive life of a cow [ગાય], it must be inseminated within 60-90 days after calving [વિયાણ]. This will enable the cow [ગાય] to produce one calf [પાડુ/વાછરડું] per year.
- Longer calving [વિયાણ] intervals have detrimental effects on lifetime milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન].
- Heat detection [વેતરની ઓળખ] is therefore a critical component of good reproductive management.

- Recording the dates of cows in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] and dates of services is necessary to predict future heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] or calving [વિયાણ] dates and to manage the cows accordingly.
# SIGNS OF HEAT [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]
- Repeated bellowing [ભાંભરવું].
- Lifting of tail.
- Swollen vulvar lips and redness of vaginal passage due to congestion.
- Thick, sticky and transparent vaginal discharge.
- Frequent urination [વારંવાર પેશાબ કરવો] (Micturition).
- Reduced feed [ચારો] intake and decreased milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ].
- Restlessness [બેચેની], smells other animals and mounts on them.
- After 10-12 hours in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], the animal [પશુ] allows a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or a cow [ગાય] to mount on her. This is the right time for carrying out AI.

# Introduction

Usually, ration of crossbred cows and high yielding buffaloes during early lactation [દૂધાળ ગાળો] is energy deficient. The animals are fed limited quantity of cultivated fodder and energy rich supplements. As a result, animals loose body weight [શરીરનું વજન] after calving [વિયાણ] at a faster rate. Under field conditions, crossbred cows and buffaloes often loose around 80-100 kg body weight [શરીરનું વજન] after calving [વિયાણ]. Such debilitated animals don't come in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], unless they fully or partially recover from the lost body weight [શરીરનું વજન]. This leads to delayed conception [ગર્ભધારણ] in animals after calving [વિયાણ], resulting into longer inter-calving interval [બે વિયાણ વચ્ચેનો ગાળો]. In addition, the animals produce less milk during this period, thus, decreased lactation [દૂધાળ ગાળો] yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ]. Overall, it is a significant economic loss to milk producers on account of less milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] and longer inter-calving interval [બે વિયાણ વચ્ચેનો ગાળો].

Raw edible oils if given beyond certain proportion as a source of fat [ફેટ] for increasing energy density of the ration may adversely affect fibre digestion and bind divalent mineral ions. Therefore, it is necessary to supplement the fats in such a form, which can provide energy without affecting fibre digestion in the rumen. This should be possible if fat [ફેટ] is supplemented in rumen protected form, which does not interfere with the fibre digestion in the rumen.

Bypass fat [બાયપાસ ફેટ] thus get digested in the abomasum at acidic pH, without interfering with the fermentative digestion in the rumen. Fat [ફેટ] supplements in this form are termed as bypass fat [બાયપાસ ફેટ], which can help in improving milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન], body condition score [શારીરિક અવસ્થાના ગુણાંક] and reproduction [પ્રજનન] efficiency [કાર્યક્ષમતા].

- Lumpy Skin Disease [ગાંઠિયો રોગ] (LSD) is a viral disease [વિષાણુથી થતો રોગ] affecting cattle [પશુ] and buffalo [ભેંસ], causing nodules on the skin and other parts of the body [બૈડા/બરડા].
- This disease is caused by a poxvirus, leading to small to large nodules appearing on the animal [પશુ]'s skin and other body [બૈડા/બરડા] parts.
- Due to this disease, other animals in contact with the infected animal [પશુ] can also become affected.
## Transmission:
- The primary mode of transmission of this disease is through insect vectors such as flies, mosquitoes, and ticks [ઇતરડી].
- Secretions from infected animals, such as blood, nasal discharge, saliva, etc., aid in the spread of the disease.
## Symptoms of the Disease:
- High fever [તાવ] (103-104°F).
- Discharge from the eyes and nose.
- Reduced feed [ચારો] intake.
- Decrease in milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન].
- General lethargy and depression in the surrounding environment [પર્યાવરણ].
- Hard nodules appear on the skin of the animal [પશુ]'s body [બૈડા/બરડા], which can be 2 to 5 cm thick. These nodules are round and firm.
- Swelling on the legs and hooves can lead to lameness [લંગડાપણું].
- Abortion [પશુ તરવાઈ જવું] may occur in pregnant [ગાભણ] animals.
- Infected animals may become infertile.

- Prevent the movement of animals from disease-affected areas.
- Isolate sick animals to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy animals.
- Keep healthy animals away from sick animals.
- Apply antiseptic ointments on wounds and ensure that flies and other insects do not come into contact with the wounds.
- Disinfectants such as Domoline (2%), Dinol (2% for 15 minutes), Sodium Hypochlorite (2-3%), and Quaternary Ammonium Compounds (0.5%) can be used for controlling the spread of the disease.

Lumpy skin disease [ગાંઠિયો રોગ] (LSD) is a viral disease [વિષાણુથી થતો રોગ] caused by the Lumpy Skin Disease [ગાંઠિયો રોગ] Virus (LSDV), which is **""characterized by the appearance of skin nodules""**. The disease is transmitted by arthropod vectors such as mosquitoes and causes high morbidity and low mortality [મૃત્યુદર] in animals. Due to this, the World Organisation for Animal [પશુ] Health (OIE) declares it as a notifiable disease. However, the virus is not zoonotic and does not infect humans through the consumption of either milk or meat.
## Occurrence and Spread:

According to a risk assessment report by the FAO, LSD was reported in Bangladesh in July 2019. In India, it was first reported in Odisha in August 2019. The disease spread to 15 other states in India within just 16 months. Later, in August 2020, the livestock [પશુઓ] sector of Maharashtra was affected by an LSD outbreak, which subsequently spread to South Gujarat and then sporadically to other parts of Gujarat. The occurrence and spread of the disease have been significant.
## Status in Gujarat till 2022:

The previous year, more than 80,000 LSD cases were reported, and vaccination [રસીકરણ] was administered to more than 380,000 animals in different districts of the state. Presently in Gujarat, LSD has been reported in over 125,000 animals across around 23 districts. So far, mortality [મૃત્યુદર] has been reported at less than 1%, while in comorbid affected animals, it has been nearly about 1%. The comparatively higher mortality [મૃત્યુદર] rate in comorbid animals is due to a hampered immune system and improper care of the affected animal [પશુ].

- Heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is a period of acceptance for mating (sexual receptivity) that normally occurs in non-pregnant [ગાભણ], pubescent heifers and non-pregnant [ગાભણ] cows.

## ANIMAL IDENTIFICATION [પશુઓની ઓળખ]
- The process of uniquely identifying an animal [પશુ] using a marking on the body [બૈડા/બરડા] of the animal [પશુ] is known as animal identification [પશુઓની ઓળખ].
- Identification of an animal [પશુ] is very important while recording any interventions on it for creation of a reliable and rich database.
- The Gol has already passed a Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals (PCICDA) Act, 2009 which makes identification of the animal [પશુ] compulsory.
- This Act has been passed by the Gol so that adequate measures are taken to be in line with international policies.
- There are various methods for identification like tattooing, branding, eartagging etc.
- Ear tagging is the most common method of identification and uses a unique number with a check digit. There are no chances of the number being duplicated.
- If applied correctly, it does not cause any problems and remains for many years on the ear of the animal [પશુ].

- INPAH is able to record the ear tag [કાનની કડી] of each animal [પશુ] registered with it along with all the details of the animal [પશુ] (breed, age, whether pregnant [ગાભણ], milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ], owner's details, village name etc.) so that a permanent passport of the animal [પશુ] is created which can be transferred or traced to any location in the country.

- **Acidic soil** has a pH below 5.5, and lime recommendations or farmyard manure, compost, and green manuring are suggested.

# SECTION I
## ANIMAL IDENTIFICATION [પશુઓની ઓળખ]
- The process of uniquely identifying an animal [પશુ] using a marking on the body [બૈડા/બરડા] of the animal [પશુ] is known as animal identification [પશુઓની ઓળખ].
- Identification of an animal [પશુ] is very important while recording any interventions on it for creation of a reliable and rich database.
- The Gol has already passed a Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals (PCICDA) Act, 2009 which makes identification of the animal [પશુ] compulsory.
- This Act has been passed by the Gol so that adequate measures are taken to be in line with international policies.
- There are various methods for identification like tattooing, branding, eartagging etc.
- Ear tagging is the most common method of identification and uses a unique number with a check digit. There are no chances of the number being duplicated.
- If applied correctly, it does not cause any problems and remains for many years on the ear of the animal [પશુ].

- INPAH is able to record the ear tag [કાનની કડી] of each animal [પશુ] registered with it along with all the details of the animal [પશુ] (breed, age, whether pregnant [ગાભણ], milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ], owner's details, village name etc.) so that a permanent passport of the animal [પશુ] is created which can be transferred or traced to any location in the country.

## Soil Health Card [આરોગ્ય કાર્ડ] Details:
- **Acidic soil** has a pH below 5.5, and lime recommendations or farmyard manure, compost, and green manuring are suggested.
- **Normal soil** has a pH between 6.5 and 7.5 and is suitable for all crops.

- **Alkaline soil** has a pH above 8.5, and gypsum recommendations are provided. Soils with a pH below 5 and above 8.5 show nutrient imbalances. Saline soils become very hard upon drying, making tillage difficult, and nutrient availability decreases. To loosen and improve such soils, the use of gypsum is essential. The important facets of animal [પશુ] health, breeding [પ્રજનન] and nutrition [પોષણ] mentioned in the previous sections should be supported by an information system for recording the activities in the field so that a rich database is created which would be beneficial both to the farmers and policy makers.

NDDB has created such a system called the Information Network for Animal [પશુ] Productivity [ઉત્પાદકતા] and Health (INAPH) which is being presently used in the field for recording various interventions in animal [પશુ] health, breeding [પ્રજનન] and nutrition [પોષણ]. A brief description of the information system and the benefits to the farmers are mentioned in the following sections:
- Section I. Animal Identification [પશુઓની ઓળખ]

# SECTION I
## ANIMAL IDENTIFICATION [પશુઓની ઓળખ]
- The process of uniquely identifying an animal [પશુ] using a marking on the body [બૈડા/બરડા] of the animal [પશુ] is known as animal identification [પશુઓની ઓળખ].
- Identification of an animal [પશુ] is very important while recording any interventions on it for creation of a reliable and rich database.
- The Gol has already passed a Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals (PCICDA) Act, 2009 which makes identification of the animal [પશુ] compulsory.
- This Act has been passed by the Gol so that adequate measures are taken to be in line with international policies.
- There are various methods for identification like tattooing, branding, eartagging etc.
- Ear tagging is the most common method of identification and uses a unique number with a check digit. There are no chances of the number being duplicated.
- If applied correctly, it does not cause any problems and remains for many years on the ear of the animal [પશુ].

- INPAH is able to record the ear tag [કાનની કડી] of each animal [પશુ] registered with it along with all the details of the animal [પશુ] (breed, age, whether pregnant [ગાભણ], milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ], owner's details, village name etc.) so that a permanent passport of the animal [પશુ] is created which can be transferred or traced to any location in the country.

# A. HEAT [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]
- Heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is a period in which female animal [પશુ] shows interest in other animals.

- Generally adult heifer [પાડી]/cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] comes in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] after every 21 days but may come in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] any time between 18/24 days.
- This period may last from 6 to 30 hours.
- To maximize productive life of a cow [ગાય], it must be inseminated within 60-90 days after calving [વિયાણ]. This will enable the cow [ગાય] to produce one calf [પાડુ/વાછરડું] per year.
- Longer calving [વિયાણ] intervals have detrimental effects on lifetime milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન].
- Heat detection [વેતરની ઓળખ] is therefore a critical component of good reproductive management.

- Recording the dates of cows in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] and dates of services is necessary to predict future heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] or calving [વિયાણ] dates and to manage the cows accordingly.
# SIGNS OF HEAT [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]
- Repeated bellowing [ભાંભરવું].
- Lifting of tail.
- Swollen vulvar lips and redness of vaginal passage due to congestion.
- Thick, sticky and transparent vaginal discharge.
- Frequent urination [વારંવાર પેશાબ કરવો] (Micturition).
- Reduced feed [ચારો] intake and decreased milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ].
- Restlessness [બેચેની], smells other animals and mounts on them.
- After 10-12 hours in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], the animal [પશુ] allows a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or a cow [ગાય] to mount on her. This is the right time for carrying out AI.
When a cow [ગાય] stands still while being mounted is the right time for insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન].
# PROPER TIME OF INSEMINATION [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

- Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (either natural service or by Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (AI)) should be given ideally after 10-12 hours, or maximum of 18 hours of first sign of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], that is, if heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is seen in the evening, inseminate in the following morning. If heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] persists in the following morning, another AI may be required on the same evening.
- If the animal [પશુ] does not become pregnant [ગાભણ], it will come into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] after 18-21 days.
- After 21 days of insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] the animal [પશુ] should be observed for symptoms of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], especially during early morning and late evening hours.

## (Toxin Binder cum Mould Inhibitor)

The mycotoxin of greatest concern to dairy industry [ડેરી ઉદ્યોગ] is aflatoxin B₁. Aflatoxin M₁ is the hydroxylated metabolite of aflatoxin B₁ and can be found in milk or milk products obtained from livestock [પશુઓ] that have ingested aflatoxin contaminated feeds & fodder, excreted within 12 hours of consumption of contaminated feeds/fodder. The presence of aflatoxin M₁ in milk is a serious regulatory concern in the majority of tropical countries, including India.

As per the FSSAI, the permissible level of aflatoxin M₁ in milk is 0.5 ppb. Aflatoxin B₁ contamination in concentrate [દાણ] feed [ચારો] varies from 15-120 ppb and average excretion of aflatoxin B₁ as M₁ in milk is 1-4%. The consumption of mycotoxin contaminated feeds by dairy animals lead to adverse effects on animal [પશુ] health, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] and consequent economic loss to the milk producers.

Higher levels of aflatoxin M₁ in milk are dangerous for human beings as aflatoxin M₁ has been reported to be carcinogenic. In view of this, restriction of aflatoxin B₁ in the ration of milk producing animals by ensuring that the level of aflatoxin M₁ does not exceed the permissible limit in milk, thereby, causing potential danger to human health. To prevent aflatoxin B₁ excretion in milk as M₁, Amul Toxi-Go-100 is premium quality and effective toxin binder cum mould inhibitor for supplementing dairy animals.

## **(4) Anaplasmosis [લોહીના પરોપજીવી]:**

The causative organisms of this disease reside within the red blood cells. It causes **fever [તાવ] and anemia** in animals. The organisms, *Anaplasma marginale*, are positioned along the inner margins of red blood cells, leading to the disease. It affects **cattle [પશુ], buffaloes, sheep, and goats**, though sheep and goats act as **reservoirs** of the pathogen. Transmission occurs via **ticks [ઇતરડી], flies, and infected blood** from one animal [પશુ] to another.
## **Symptoms:**
- Anaplasmosis [લોહીના પરોપજીવી] is primarily observed in **adult livestock [પશુઓ]**.
- Animals **under 18 months** may contract the disease but exhibit **milder symptoms**.
- In adult animals, symptoms appear **4 weeks post-infection [ચેપ]**.
- **Initial stage:**
- High fever [તાવ]
- Proliferation of *Anaplasma* within red blood cells
- Gradual destruction of RBCs, leading to **~70% loss within a week**
- **Consequences of RBC destruction:**
- Severe **anemia**, weakening the animal [પશુ]
- **Loss of appetite [ભૂખ]**
- **Respiratory distress [શ્વાસમાં તકલીફ]** due to anemia
- **Significant reduction in milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ]** in affected cows
- **Abortion [પશુ તરવાઈ જવું]** in pregnant [ગાભણ] animals
- In **peracute cases**, death may occur **within a day**
- Recovered animals take **a long time** to return to normal health.
- **Mortality [મૃત્યુદર] rate: ~80%** without timely treatment.
## **Treatment:**
- If symptoms are observed, **immediately contact the nearest veterinarian**.
- Administer **Berenil or Oxytetracycline injections** along with **liver tonics**.
- **Isolate sick animals** from healthy ones.

- Vaccinate female calves (not male calves) between 4–8 months of age.
- Only one vaccination [રસીકરણ] is required in their lifetime to protect against brucellosis [ચેપી ગર્ભપાત (બ્રુસેલોસીસ)].
- Any abortion [પશુ તરવાઈ જવું] from the 5th month onward should be suspected as brucellosis [ચેપી ગર્ભપાત (બ્રુસેલોસીસ)].

- Ideally, such animals should be culled. If culling [નકામા પશુને અલગ કરવા] is not possible, isolate the animal [પશુ] immediately for a minimum of 20 days after calving [વિયાણ]/abortion [પશુ તરવાઈ જવું].

- The aborted fetus [ગર્ભ], placenta [મેલી/જર], contaminated bedding, feed [ચારો], etc., should be buried (at least 4 feet deep) after liberal sprinkling of lime. - Disinfect the shed after isolating the aborted animal [પશુ].

- While the animal [પશુ] is in isolation, disinfect lochial discharges (which also contain high bacterial loads) daily with 1–2% NaOH or 5% sodium hypochlorite (bleach) solution until discharges cease (usually by 10–15 days).

- The disease in humans is curable if a proper treatment regimen is followed.
**Vaccinate 4–8-month-old female calves once—protect them for life.**

Since your cow is 8 months pregnant, she is entering the most critical phase. It is highly recommended to use a specialized pregnancy feed.
*   **Recommended Feed:** **Amul Pregnancy Feed**
*   **Purpose:** Specially designed for the last two months of gestation to develop the udder, improve immunity, and reduce the risk of milk fever and mastitis.
*   **Dosage:** Feed **1.5 to 2.0 kg per cow per day** during the last two months of pregnancy. Give this in dry form only.
*   **General Daily Requirements for Pregnant Animals:**
*   **Green Fodder:** 15–20 kg
*   **Dry Fodder:** 4–5 kg
*   **Compound Cattle Feed:** 2–3 kg
*   **Oil Cake:** 1 kg
*   **Mineral Mixture:** 50 g
**Key Tips for Higher Yield:**

1.  **Avoid Sudden Drying-Off:** If you are still milking the cow, do not stop abruptly. Gradually reduce milking sessions over 6–9 days to avoid udder edema, which can lower milk production after calving.

2.  **Post-Calving Care:** For the first 2–3 days after calving, provide a light, palatable diet such as warm rice gruel, jaggery, and ginger to help the cow recover from stress and ensure early removal of the placenta.

3.  **Clean Water:** Ensure the cow has constant access to fresh, clean drinking water.","After your cow calves, it is important to offer energy-rich and easily digestible feed to help her recover and increase milk production. Continue this special feed for about 10–15 days, gradually reducing it as you increase regular fodder and concentrate.
After the initial period, focus on:
- Plenty of green fodder (15–20 kg daily) and dry fodder (6 kg daily)
- Leguminous fodder (like lucerne or cowpea) mixed with non-leguminous fodder

- Supplement with quality cattle feed or concentrates based on the cow's milk yield. Include bypass protein and bypass fat supplements if available (such as Amul Nutri Energia) to boost milk yield and energy.
- Provide mineral mixture and salt licks to meet micronutrient needs
- Ensure continuous access to clean drinking water

### Types of Green Fodder [લીલો ચારો]
1) **Cereal fodder**: – Jowar (sorghum [જુવાર]), maize, oats [ઓટ્સ (જવ)], guinea grass, Napier grass, para grass, etc.
2) **Leguminous fodder**: – Lucerne [રજકો], berseem, cowpea [ચોળી], peas, gram, guar, etc.

Leguminous fodder contains higher amounts of protein [પ્રોટીન] and calcium [કેલ્શિયમ] compared to cereal fodder. Therefore, it is essential to feed [ચારો] leguminous fodder to growing, pregnant [ગાભણ], and weak animals. Cereal fodder has a higher proportion of carbohydrates, resulting in a higher total digestible nutrient content. Thus, leguminous fodder is protein [પ્રોટીન]-rich, while cereal fodder is energy-rich. However, feeding only leguminous fodder may cause bloating in animals, so it is necessary to mix leguminous and cereal fodder. Feeding raw green jowar can cause poisoning in animals due to the presence of hydrocyanic acid. Therefore, it is advisable not to feed [ચારો] such fodder and to cut jowar after it has fully matured. Green fodder [લીલો ચારો] contains 70 to 80% water, meaning that 100 kg of green fodder [લીલો ચારો] provides 20 to 30 kg of dry matter [સૂકો પદાર્થ] to the animal [પશુ]. Therefore, 3 to 5 kg of green fodder [લીલો ચારો] should be given in place of 1 kg of dry fodder [સુકો ચારો].
### (2) Concentrate [દાણ]

Feed [ચારો] materials with less than 18% fiber [રેસા] and a high proportion of nutrients are called concentrates. Maize, jowar, wheat bran [ઘઉંનું થૂલું], sesame, linseed, cottonseed, groundnut cake [મગફળીનો ખોળ], legume husks, and rice polish [ચોખાનું કુશળ], among others, fall under the category of concentrates. The natural diet of animals is roughage. However, due to scientific breeding [પ્રજનન] and rearing, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in dairy animals has increased, necessitating a higher intake of nutrients. These nutrients cannot be fully provided by roughage alone, leading to the need for feeding concentrates. Thus, concentrates are not the primary feed [ચારો] for animals but a supplementary feed [ચારો]. Concentrates should be fed to meet the nutritional requirements that are not fulfilled by roughage.

# 1.1.1 Leguminous Hay

Good legume hay possesses many characteristics that make it especially valuable for dairy cattle [પશુ]. It has a higher percentage of digestible nutrients. It contains more digestible proteins due to its high protein content [પ્રોટીનનું પ્રમાણ]. Furthermore, the proteins in legumes [કઠોળ વર્ગનો ચારો] are of superior quality compared to proteins from other plants. Well-cured legume hays are richer in vitamins [વિટામિન્સ]. Feeding is the major component of cost of milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન], accounting for 55-60% of the total cost of milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન]. Therefore, judicious feeding is the most important pillar of economical dairying. The dairy animals must be fed with a balanced ration [સંતુલિત આહાર] incorporating all the nutrients (energy, proteins, minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો] and vitamins [વિટામિન્સ]) in right proportions keeping in view the requirements of the animal [પશુ]. Dairy cows and buffaloes of an average body weight [શરીરનું વજન] of about 500 kg require between 12.5 and 15 kg of dry matter [સૂકો પદાર્થ] daily. For better productivity [ઉત્પાદકતા] feeding of both cereal and leguminous fodders in 50: 50 ratio should be preferred. It may be mentioned that the cost of milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] is always less if major chunk of the daily ration of the dairy animal [પશુ] comprises green fodders as concentrates are a costly feed [ચારો] item. This category includes pulses, their by-products, and oilseed by-products.

## Pulses:– Though primarily used in human diets, they can be included in livestock [પશુઓ] feed [ચારો] when available at low cost, such as mung, moth, pigeon pea, akad, chickpea, cowpea [ચોળી], etc. They contain approximately 20–30% protein [પ્રોટીન].

## Pulse By-Products:– When pulses are milled into dal, the by-product obtained is chuni (husked pulse residue). Different chunis contain approximately 16–30% protein [પ્રોટીન] and 5–15% fiber [રેસા]. The protein [પ્રોટીન] and fiber [રેસા] content depend on the proportion of pulse fragments and husks in the chuni.

## Oilseed Cake:– Includes cakes from cottonseed, groundnut, copra, soybean, linseed, mustard, sunflower, karki, sesame, etc. Oilseed cake is considered an excellent protein [પ્રોટીન]-rich feed [ચારો] for livestock [પશુઓ]. The oil content in cake is negligible. Cottonseed, karki, and sunflower cakes contain higher fiber [રેસા]. Most cakes contain approximately 22–45% protein [પ્રોટીન]. Maize cake has lower protein [પ્રોટીન] but swells when soaked, increasing bulk and palatability [સ્વાદિષ્ટતા]. It contains 2–10% oil, providing energy.

This disease spreads very rapidly. # A. FOOT-AND-MOUTH DISEASE (FMD [ખરવા મોવાસા])
- A highly contagious viral disease [વિષાણુથી થતો રોગ]
- Spreads through contact, contaminated water, feed [ચારો], and air.
- The disease is rarely fatal for adults; however, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન], fertility in females, and draft power of males are severely impaired for life after recovery [સાજા થવું].
- Usually fatal in calves.
- Also affects sheep, goats (usually subclinically and are maintenance hosts), and pigs, which are amplification hosts (multiply the virus up to 3,000-fold).
## SYMPTOMS
- Foot lesions
- Tongue lesions
- Dental pad lesions
- Udder [બાવલું] lesions
- Drastic drop in milk [દૂધમાં ઘટાડો] production and working capacity (draft animals).
- Fever [તાવ] and serous nasal discharge with excessive salivation.
- Vesicles may be seen on the tongue, dental pad, lips, gums, etc.
- Vesicles in the interdigital cleft may lead to lameness [લંગડાપણું].
- Lesions on the teats may lead to mastitis [આઉનો/બાવલાનો સોજો].
- Loss of condition may persist even after recovery [સાજા થવું].
## PREVENTION
- Vaccinate animals aged 4 months and above every 6 months.
- Infected animals should be immediately isolated, as all excretions and secretions from infected animals contain the virus.
- All feed [ચારો] and fodder in contact with infected animals should be destroyed.
- All equipment used should be cleaned and disinfected with a 4% sodium carbonate solution or as recommended by a veterinarian.
- Healthy animals should not be handled by persons in contact with infected animals.
- The infected premises should be disinfected with a 4% sodium carbonate solution or with a disinfectant [સાફસફાઈની દવા] recommended by a veterinarian.
- Vaccinating sheep, goats, and pigs helps control the disease more effectively.
- Promptly informing authorities enables them to initiate control measures early, limiting the spread of the disease.
## MANAGEMENT OF FMD [ખરવા મોવાસા]
- Treatment is only symptomatic; the disease will run its course.
- Emollients may be applied to lesions to soothe pain.
- Consult a veterinarian for appropriate advice.
- Vaccinate your animals regularly against FMD [ખરવા મોવાસા] to avoid economic losses.

Vaccines are primarily of two types: **live** and **killed (inactivated)**.

- **Live Vaccines**: These contain live but weakened disease-causing organisms that have lost their ability to cause disease. ## **Subject:– Ensuring proper maintenance of paper-recorded milk temperature in milk collection centers...**

With reference to the above subject, it has come to our notice that during the milk collection process, employees of the milk union are inadvertently allowing discrepancies in the handling of milk by farmers. It is imperative to prevent such practices and ensure that the paper-recorded temperature of milk is accurately maintained. Below are the key points for review, and necessary actions must be implemented in the milk union accordingly:

(1) **After milk is poured into the bulk milk cooler (BMC), the temperature of the milk must be maintained at 3.8°C [માટી ખસવી] or below until it is dispatched. The union must ensure that employees strictly adhere to this protocol.**
(2) **Until the milk temperature reaches 3.8°C [માટી ખસવી]...**
- The **agitator motor (impeller)** must be kept running continuously, and constant monitoring [દેખરેખ/નિરીક્ષણ] is required.
- Regularly check whether the **compressor’s cooling issues** (such as overheating) are being addressed.
- Ensure that the **temperature meter** accurately reflects the milk temperature and take corrective action if deviations are observed.
(3) **For checking the temperature of milk in the BMC tank, a Celsius digital thermometer [થર્મોમીટર] must be used. Mercury thermometers should not be used.**

(4) **Once the milk temperature reaches 3.8°C [માટી ખસવી], collect a sample from the upper layer of the BMC tank (using the main lid) and verify the temperature using a digital thermometer [થર્મોમીટર].** If the thermometer [થર્મોમીટર] shows a temperature higher than 3.8°C [માટી ખસવી], immediately notify the union so that **temperature indicator depression** can be addressed promptly.

# Chaff Cutter [ચાફ કટર]

Farmers mostly feed [ચારો] animals whole stalks of bajra [બાજરી] (pearl millet) and jowar (sorghum [જુવાર]). Some livestock [પશુઓ] owners cut them into two or three pieces. Since the pieces are long, animals struggle to eat them easily, and approximately **20 to 30%** of the fodder is wasted and ends up in the dung heap. Animals consume the dry leaves of jowar and bajra [બાજરી] stalks but leave the stems untouched. The nutrients in these stems go to waste. Additionally, about **30%** (i.e., **3 kg out of 10 kg** of fodder) is discarded in the dung heap instead of being digested by the animal [પશુ]. Economically, this means we waste **₹12** (at ₹4 per kg for 3 kg) per day. In today’s inflationary times, this loss is unacceptable. Losing **₹4,380 per year** is not justified.

If jowar and bajra [બાજરી] stalks are cut into smaller pieces, animals can consume the entire fodder without waste, reducing fodder loss. Farmers use **electric chaff cutters** to make small fodder pieces.

### 2. Sexual Reproduction [પ્રજનન] - Through the Process of Mating

This condition of the manure is only obtained when urine is drained away immediately and a prescribed amount of bedding like straw [કડબ/ભૂસું] or sawdust is used. Manure with less than 20% solids has the consistency of thick slurry. It should be collected in a tank or pit but is too thick to handle effectively with pumps. # 5. Importance of Water in Animal Husbandry [પશુપાલન]
## Water Management for Livestock [પશુઓ]:-

We all know that water is essential for life. However, in livestock [પશુઓ], water directly impacts the digestive system and milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન]. Generally, an animal [પશુ] requires **10 to 12% of its body weight [શરીરનું વજન]** in water for maintenance. Additionally, water requirements vary based on seasons (such as winter and summer) and the type of feed [ચારો] provided—whether dry or green fodder [લીલો ચારો]. For every liter of milk produced, an additional **3 to 4 liters of water** should be provided. Furthermore, for every kilogram of dry fodder [સુકો ચારો], an extra **4 to 5 liters of water** should be given.

It is essential to ensure that livestock [પશુઓ] have access to **clean drinking water 24 hours a day**. When constructing a permanent shed (*paki gamash*), arrange it so that one side has a water trough and the other side can be used for feeding. If possible, install a tap connected to the water pipe filling the trough to facilitate refilling. The water pipe supplying the troughs should come from a larger tank, which should be connected to the shed’s overhead tank. Install a **ballcock** on the pipe supplying water to the larger tank. Smaller troughs in the shed can be filled by opening the tap. The **overhead tank (water tank)** in the shed should be of an appropriate size—considering that in emergencies (such as power supply issues or borewell motor failures), it should hold enough water to last at least **three days**. The tank’s capacity should be calculated as:
**(Number of animals × Daily water requirement per animal [પશુ] × 3)**.

### **Home Remedies for Bloat (Tympany)**
**Important:** If the animal is severely bloated, do not allow it to lie down or provide water to drink.
**1. Oil-Based Mixtures:**
*   **Simple Oil:** Administer 300–500 ml of coconut, vegetable, or peanut oil once a day for 2–3 days.
*   **Oil with Turpentine:** Mix 300–500 grams of edible oil (mustard, sesame, or cottonseed) with 20–30 ml of turpentine oil and administer orally.
*   **Specialized Mixture:** Some recommendations suggest a mixture of 500 ml vegetable oil, 100 ml turpentine oil, 100 g rock salt, and 30 g asafoetida (hing).
**2. Herbal & Kitchen Remedies:**

*   **Powdered Mixture:** Mix 500 g edible oil with 25 g powdered asafoetida (hing), 50 g ajwain (carom seeds), 50 g sanchal (rock salt), and 50 g sunth (dry ginger). Administer via a tube and then walk the animal.
*   **Banana Leaves:** For very mild cases, feeding 4–6 banana leaves may help.
*   **Detergent Solution:** One tablespoon of detergent dissolved in half a liter of water can be given once.
**3. Other Options:**
*   **Epsom Salt:** Dissolve 400–500 g of Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) in water to induce purging.

## Symptoms:

Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD [ખરવા મોવાસા]) is a severe viral and contagious disease [સંસર્ગજન્ય રોગ] observed in cloven-hoofed animals [ફાટેલા ખુરવાળા પશુઓ] (cattle [પશુ], buffalo [ભેંસ], goats, sheep, etc.). Excessive salivation occurs, making it extremely difficult for the animal [પશુ] to eat fodder. The hooves may develop lesions, leading to lameness [લંગડાપણું]. Pregnant [ગાભણ] animals have a high risk of **abortion [પશુ તરવાઈ જવું]**, and they may face difficulties in conceiving afterward. In young animals, the virus damages the **heart muscles**, resulting in a very high mortality [મૃત્યુદર] rate.
## Spread:

This disease spreads very rapidly. It transmits to healthy animals through **contact with infected animals** or contaminated **fodder, utensils, water, etc.** The disease can also spread via wind in **humid conditions at night**. The virus is present in the **saliva, urine, milk, and dung** of infected animals.

The virus can survive for **up to one year** in enclosures where infected animals were kept. It can remain alive in **fodder for 3–4 months** and on **animal [પશુ] hair for up to one month**, potentially infecting other healthy animals.
Even after recovery [સાજા થવું], **cattle [પશુ]/buffalo [ભેંસ]** may carry the virus in their bodies for **6 to 24 months** and can transmit the disease to other animals.

The bacteria [બેક્ટેરિયા] enter the animal [પશુ]'s body [બૈડા/બરડા] through the respiratory and digestive systems. Symptoms appear within 1 to 2 days of bacterial entry. The primary symptoms are observed in the throat region. Initial symptoms include loss of appetite [ભૂખ] and fever [તાવ]. Subsequently, the animal [પશુ] experiences difficulty breathing, producing a wheezing sound. Swelling occurs from beneath the jaw to the throat, neck [ગળું], and dewlap (extending to the front legs). The animal [પશુ]'s tongue swells and hangs out of the mouth, with saliva dripping continuously, eventually leading to death.
**Treatment:**

Hemorrhagic Septicemia is a severe and fatal disease. At the first sign of symptoms, a veterinarian should be called immediately for appropriate treatment to save the animal [પશુ]. Since this disease is contagious, precautions should be taken to prevent its spread to other animals.

Due to its contagious nature, infected animals should be immediately isolated from healthy ones. Feed [ચારો], fodder, and living areas should also be kept separate. Vaccination [રસીકરણ] can prevent Hemorrhagic Septicemia. The first vaccine should be administered to calves over 4 months old, followed by a second dose 3 months after the first. ## Foot and Mouth Disease [ખરવા-મોવાસા] (FMD [ખરવા મોવાસા])

- This is a highly contagious viral disease [વિષાણુથી થતો રોગ] that spreads rapidly. While livestock [પશુઓ] rarely die from it, the disease significantly impacts their productivity [ઉત્પાદકતા] and working capacity, leading to substantial economic losses.
- The disease affects cloven-hoofed ruminants such as cows, buffaloes, bulls, sheep, goats, etc.
- The virus can survive for long periods outside the host on grass, meat, soil, feed [ચારો], etc., and enters the animal [પશુ]’s body [બૈડા/બરડા] through air, water, or food, causing the disease.
## Symptoms
- After 3 to 4 days, the animal [પશુ] develops a fever [તાવ] ranging from 104°F to 106°F.
- Blisters appear in the mouth, between the hooves, or in both locations.
- The animal [પશુ] is unable to eat, drinks water frequently, and stops ruminating.
- Due to ulcers in the mouth, saliva drips, and the animal [પશુ] grinds its teeth. These ulcers appear on the tongue, inside the lips, and on the jaws.
- Blisters in the hooves cause difficulty in walking.
## Treatment
- Treatment is administered based on the symptoms.
- Consult a veterinary doctor [પશુચિકિત્સક].
- Clean the hooves with warm water mixed with alum or potassium permanganate [પોટેશિયમ પરમેંગેનેટ] (PP) (1:1000).
- If cracks develop in the hooves, use turpentine oil [ટર્પેન્ટાઈન તેલ].
- Apply a mixture of turmeric [હળદર] and butter inside the mouth and avoid dry grass.
- Dig a pit approximately 2 meters long, 1.25 meters wide, and 20 cm deep, fill it with a 4.5% soda solution, and make the animals walk through it.
## Post-Recovery [સાજા થવું] Complications
- After recovering from the disease, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] decreases, and the animal [પશુ] may not produce milk at full capacity.
- The reproductive capacity of the animal [પશુ] is also adversely affected, making conception [ગર્ભધારણ] difficult.
- The animal [પશુ] may shiver even in cold weather.
- Blisters between the hooves may develop into maggots.
- Other symptoms include anemia, excessive hair growth, swelling on the dewlap, etc.

Such infectious diseases are highly dangerous; once they begin in a village, they spread very rapidly, and controlling them becomes extremely difficult. Therefore, efforts should be made to prevent the spread of such infectious diseases before they occur.

The root cause of infectious diseases is bacteria [બેક્ટેરિયા], viruses, and parasites, which can be observed using a microscope. Thus, these pathogens can be studied in detail in a laboratory. A detailed description of important infectious diseases is as follows:

### **Causes:**

The virus responsible for this disease has **7 serotypes**, with numerous subtypes. In our country, the disease is primarily caused by **serotypes A, O, C [માટી ખસવી], and Asia subtypes**. Due to its rapid spread, if one animal [પશુ] in a herd [ધણ] contracts the disease, nearly all others become infected. The bacteria [બેક્ટેરિયા] enter the animal [પશુ]'s body [બૈડા/બરડા] through the respiratory and digestive systems. Symptoms appear within 1 to 2 days of bacterial entry. Hemorrhagic Septicemia is a severe and fatal disease. At the first sign of symptoms, a veterinarian should be called immediately for appropriate treatment to save the animal [પશુ]. Since this disease is contagious, precautions should be taken to prevent its spread to other animals.

Due to its contagious nature, infected animals should be immediately isolated from healthy ones. Feed [ચારો], fodder, and living areas should also be kept separate. ### Risk Analysis

The primary aim of risk analysis is to provide an objective and defensible method of assessing disease risks associated with any farm-related procedure or activity. The four components of risk analysis are:
- **Hazard identification** – Identifying pathogenic agents linked to an importation that could produce adverse consequences.
- **Risk assessment** – Evaluating hazards associated with an importation, procedure, exposure scenarios, and available data.
- **Risk management** – Deciding on and implementing measures to achieve appropriate protection while minimizing negative effects.
- **Risk communication** – Sharing information and opinions on hazard identification, risk assessment, and management measures with decision-makers.

# Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

This is a scientific method in which semen from a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] is collected artificially, tested in a laboratory, and then deposited into the reproductive tract of a female in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] using scientific instruments.
## Why Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]?
- For rapid improvement of livestock [પશુઓ] breeds
- To achieve higher milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in less time
- For extensive use of semen from proven high-quality bulls
## Laws of Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

- Naturally, a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or buffalo [ભેંસ] can impregnate about 100 females in a year. Through artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], more than 2000 females can be impregnated in a year. Thus, the use of high-quality bulls or buffaloes accelerates breed improvement.
- Fewer bulls or buffaloes are required, allowing for the selection of the best males.
- When cows or buffaloes are naturally impregnated, diseased males can spread diseases to many females. In artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], the risk of disease transmission is eliminated.
- During insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], the female's reproductive organs are examined, allowing for the treatment of any defects.

- When a female is in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], the livestock [પશુઓ] owner does not need to search for a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or buffalo [ભેંસ]. A trained insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] technician can perform the insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] on time using semen from high-quality males.
- Records of insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] dates facilitate accurate pregnancy [ગર્ભ] testing and planning.
- Semen from high-quality bulls or buffaloes stored in semen centers can be used even after their death.
- Semen from high-quality livestock [પશુઓ] can be transported to any location, making good quality semen available in villages at minimal cost.
- Facilitates crossbreeding [સંકરણ].
- Simplifies the impregnation process and increases the conception rate [ગર્ભાધાન દર].
## Precautions in Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]
1. Selection of bull [સાંઢ/આખલો]/buffalo [ભેંસ]
2. Proper semen collection method
3. Appropriate time for artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]
4. Complete hygiene during the artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] process
5. Proper timing for performing artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]
Conducting insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] during the middle phase (Standing Heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]) increases the likelihood of the animal [પશુ] becoming pregnant [ગાભણ].

# Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

This is a scientific method in which semen from a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] is collected artificially, tested in a laboratory, and then deposited into the reproductive tract of a female in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] using scientific instruments.
## Why Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]?
- For rapid improvement of livestock [પશુઓ] breeds
- To achieve higher milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in less time
- For extensive use of semen from proven high-quality bulls
## Laws of Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]

- Naturally, a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or buffalo [ભેંસ] can impregnate about 100 females in a year. Through artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], more than 2000 females can be impregnated in a year. Thus, the use of high-quality bulls or buffaloes accelerates breed improvement.
- Fewer bulls or buffaloes are required, allowing for the selection of the best males.
- When cows or buffaloes are naturally impregnated, diseased males can spread diseases to many females. In artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], the risk of disease transmission is eliminated.
- During insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], the female's reproductive organs are examined, allowing for the treatment of any defects.

- When a female is in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], the livestock [પશુઓ] owner does not need to search for a bull [સાંઢ/આખલો] or buffalo [ભેંસ]. A trained insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] technician can perform the insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] on time using semen from high-quality males.
- Records of insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] dates facilitate accurate pregnancy [ગર્ભ] testing and planning.
- Semen from high-quality bulls or buffaloes stored in semen centers can be used even after their death.
- Semen from high-quality livestock [પશુઓ] can be transported to any location, making good quality semen available in villages at minimal cost.
- Facilitates crossbreeding [સંકરણ].
- Simplifies the impregnation process and increases the conception rate [ગર્ભાધાન દર].

2. Provide information about the previous inseminations of the animal [પશુ] being inseminated. If necessary, examine the animal [પશુ]'s rectum to check the reproductive organs.
3. Use a **Graz 631** straw [કડબ/ભૂસું] pipette to transfer the semen into the **Nitrogen Container**.

11. Control the animal [પશુ] properly during insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] and use iodine on the vulva.
12. Perform insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] preferably in shaded areas, either in the early morning or late evening.

## Pregnancy Diagnosis [ખાલી ગાભણ તપાસ] (PD)
### **(1) Genetic Factors:**

Hereditary or congenital defects in the reproductive tract can impact fertility. If such defects are severe in animals, infertility [વંધ્યત્વ] may manifest during the first insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] cycle. In cattle [પશુ], these defects can be subtle yet serious, making it difficult to identify infertility causes [વંધ્યત્વના કારણો]. However, identifying and culling [નકામા પશુને અલગ કરવા] affected animals can help mitigate economic losses.
### **(2) Internal Factors:**

Infertility [વંધ્યત્વ] can also stem from internal issues affecting individual animals, such as nutritional deficiencies or excesses, and internal diseases that may lead to repeat breeding [ઠરતું નથી, ઉથલા મારવા ઝેભની, ગાભણ રહેતી નથી]. In such cases, appropriate treatment should be administered promptly.
### **(3) Errors in Heat Detection [વેતરની ઓળખ]:**

If proper heat detection [વેતરની ઓળખ] is not performed in animals, issues like missed estrus cycles, untimely insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], and heat stress [ગરમીનો તણાવ] can lead to infertility [વંધ્યત્વ] and repeat breeding [ઠરતું નથી, ઉથલા મારવા ઝેભની, ગાભણ રહેતી નથી]. Key considerations include:
- The average duration of estrus (heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]) is **18 to 24 hours**.
- Ovulation [બીજ છૂટું પડવું/અંડપાત] occurs **12 hours after the end of estrus**.
- Sperm viability lasts **48 hours**, while the ovum remains viable for **12–24 hours**.

- The best time for artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (AI) is **12 to 18 hours after the onset of estrus**.
- Observing behavioral signs of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is essential to ensure timely insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન].
### **(4) Improper Artificial Insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] Techniques:**

Inadequate semen extension, failure to maintain proper cooling of semen, or insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] without proper thawing of frozen semen [થીજવેલું વીર્ય] can also contribute to infertility [વંધ્યત્વ].

Post-ovulation [બીજ છૂટું પડવું/અંડપાત], the egg retains its fertilization capacity for **6 to 8 hours**. Similarly, sperm deposited in the uterus [ગર્ભાશય] can retain fertilization capacity for approximately **18 to 24 hours**. Therefore, the highest probability of conception [ગર્ભધારણ] is achieved when insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] is performed **12 to 16 hours after the first signs of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]** or during the **last 2/3 of the estrous cycle**. ### 1. યોગ્ય બ્રીડિંગ તકનીકો
*   **ચોક્કસ રીતે માદામાં આવેલી ગરમીની ઓળખ:** ખાતરી કરો કે ગાય સ્પષ્ટ રીતે માદામાં આવી છે. જો માદામાં આવવાના ચિહ્નો સ્પષ્ટ ન હોય, તો સમન્વય (સમયસર કૃત્રિમ ગર્ભાધાન) ધ્યાનમાં લો.
*   **યોગ્ય સમય:** કૃત્રિમ ગર્ભાધાન (AI) માદાના સમયગાળા દરમિયાન કરો, સામાન્ય રીતે માદાની શરૂઆત પછી **12 થી 18 કલાક** પછી.

*   **ગુણવત્તા નિયંત્રણ:** ઉચ્ચ ગુણવત્તાવાળા, સક્રિય શુક્રાણુઓનો ઉપયોગ કરો. જો સ્થિર શુક્રાણુનો ઉપયોગ કરી રહ્યા હો, તો ખાતરી કરો કે સ્ટ્રોને ગરમ પાણીમાં (35–40°C) ઓછામાં ઓછા 30 સેકન્ડ માટે યોગ્ય રીતે ઓગાળવામાં આવે.
*   **સ્વચ્છતા:** AI દરમિયાન કડક જંતુરહિત પરિસ્થિતિઓ જાળવો જેથી જનનાંગ માર્ગના ચેપને અટકાવી શકાય.
### 2. પોષણ વ્યવસ્થાપન
*   **સંતુલિત આહાર:** ઊર્જાથી ભરપૂર, સંતુલિત આહાર પ્રદાન કરો જેમાં પૂરતા પ્રમાણમાં લીલો અને સૂકો ચારો હોય.

૫. યોગ્ય કૃત્રિમ ગર્ભાધાન તકનીક: ખાતરી કરો કે કૃત્રિમ ગર્ભાધાન તાલીમ પામેલા કર્મચારી દ્વારા ગુણવત્તાયુક્ત શુક્રાણુનો ઉપયોગ કરીને કરવામાં આવે.

While the use of chelated minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો] is not yet widespread in our country, efforts are needed to promote their adoption.

- For animals in extreme heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], perform a second artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] after 24 hours.

1. If there are complications during calving [વિયાણ], seek a doctor’s assistance.
2. If the afterbirth does not expel naturally within 24 hours post-calving [વિયાણ પછી], call a veterinarian to remove it and provide treatment.

4. In the summer season, ensure relief from heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] for the animal [પશુ] by:
- Covering [ઢાંકવું] the shed with proper thatching.
- Applying white lime (chuna) to reflect heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું].
- Arranging for coolers and fans if possible.
5. Perform timely artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] for animals in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું].
6. After artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], closely monitor for signs of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] between **18 to 20 days** and **36 to 40 days**.

## Challenges in Heat Detection [વેતરની ઓળખ]:
### (a) Silent Heat [શાંત વેતર] (Mungi Garmi):

When a female animal [પશુ] does not exhibit any visible signs of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], it is referred to as **silent heat [શાંત વેતર], quiet heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], or subdued heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]**. The primary issue is the lack of overt behavioral signs, making it difficult for farmers to detect estrus. Due to variations in animal behavior [પશુની વર્તણૂક] and individual temperament, continuous observation is necessary to identify silent heat [શાંત વેતર] symptoms. For dairy farmers focused on regular milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] and herd [ધણ] expansion, early diagnosis [નિદાન] and appropriate management of silent heat [શાંત વેતર] are crucial.

To address silent heat [શાંત વેતર], the use of **teaser bulls (vasectomized bulls)** is recommended to confirm the onset of the estrous cycle. Studies indicate that **20-27%** of animals exhibit silent heat [શાંત વેતર], and even when teaser bulls are used, **13-15%** of animals may fail to show a clear estrous response, necessitating veterinary intervention.
### (b) Irregular Estrus Cycle (Rutukāṇ/Ṛtuchakra):
The estrous cycle in animals can be classified as:
- **Short (6-12 days)**
- **Normal (12-24 days)**
- **Long (24-41 days)**
Similarly, the duration of the estrous cycle may vary:
- **Very short (≤8 days)**
- **Short (8-12 days)**
- **Moderately short (12-18 days)**
- **Normal (18-24 days)**
- **Long (≥25 days)**
Animals with **short or long estrous cycles** (excluding normal cycles) may require veterinary consultation to induce estrus, as such irregularities can indicate underlying reproductive disorders.

# Ideal Calving Interval [બે વિયાણ વચ્ચેનો ગાળો]

## Factors Affecting Livestock [પશુઓ] Productivity [ઉત્પાદકતા] During the Hot Season:
### (1) Temperature and Humidity Levels:

Increased temperature and humidity levels negatively impact livestock [પશુઓ] productivity [ઉત્પાદકતા]. Due to high temperature and humidity, animals stand for longer periods to expel excess body [બૈડા/બરડા] heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] through respiration.
### (2) High Radiation:

During the hot season, solar radiation on the animals' bodies causes the skin to absorb heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], increasing body temperature [શરીરનું તાપમાન]. To dissipate this heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], animals breathe rapidly. As a result, heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]-stressed dairy animals consume up to 20% less feed [ચારો]. Due to reduced feed [ચારો] intake in the hot season, the energy produced in the body [બૈડા/બરડા] decreases significantly.
### (3) Excessive Winds:

While low temperatures and cool winds do not affect milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન], high temperatures combined with hot winds adversely impact milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] capacity. The energy produced by livestock [પશુઓ] during the hot season is a major cause of stress [તણાવ]. When humidity exceeds 72%, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] begins to decline. # Silage (Preservation [જાળવણી] of Green Fodder [લીલો ચારો])
## What is Silage?

Silage is a method of preserving green fodder [લીલો ચારો] in a succulent state when its nutrient content is high, allowing it to be stored for extended periods. Similar to how grains are used in animal [પશુ] feed [ચારો] during scarcity or when fresh fodder is unavailable, silage serves as a preserved form of green fodder [લીલો ચારો] for livestock [પશુઓ].
## Silage Preparation Process:

- Silage should be prepared when green fodder [લીલો ચારો] is abundant during the rainy season and cannot be fully utilized immediately, or when fodder growth continues even after meeting the livestock [પશુઓ]'s immediate needs.

- The optimal time for silage preparation is when the crop is at the right maturity stage for harvesting [કાપણી/લણણી]. This ensures that during the year, the same land can produce additional fodder to sustain livestock [પશુઓ].

- Harvesting [કાપણી/લણણી] green fodder [લીલો ચારો] at its peak nutrient content and converting it into silage ensures livestock [પશુઓ] receive high-quality feed [ચારો]. Without proper silage knowledge [જ્ઞાન/માહિતી], one might resort to using overripe or mature fodder, which has lower nutrient content and fails to maintain animal [પશુ] health.
- It is essential to chop the fodder into small pieces using a chopper to facilitate proper packing.
- Green fodder [લીલો ચારો] should be cut, chopped (chopped into small pieces), and packed daily in layers. After packing, it should be sealed daily to prevent air exposure.

- Silage allows green fodder [લીલો ચારો] to be stored for extended periods, ensuring its use during fodder scarcity and providing high-quality green fodder [લીલો ચારો] to livestock [પશુઓ] throughout the year.
- Nutrients like carotene (Vitamin A), which are lost in dry fodder [સુકો ચારો], and other nutrients that degrade during drying, are preserved in higher quantities due to silage preparation.
- Silage preparation enhances the digestibility [પાચનશક્તિ] and palatability [સ્વાદિષ્ટતા] of fodder.
- Silage requires less storage space compared to dry fodder [સુકો ચારો].
- Dry fodder [સુકો ચારો] storage carries a risk of accidental fires, whereas silage storage does not.

- In areas with limited grazing land [ચરિયાણ] or during droughts, purchasing green fodder [લીલો ચારો] can be expensive. Preparing silage ensures a year-round supply of green fodder [લીલો ચારો]. (For example, 15 kg of good-quality silage can replace 3 kg of dry fodder [સુકો ચારો].)

**Local name:** Lucerne [રજકો]

Lucerne [રજકો] is a valuable leguminous forage and hay crop generally grown in areas where water supply is inadequate for berseem. Its deeper root system makes it well-adapted to dry areas with irrigation [પિયત] facilities. It continues to supply nutritious fodder for **3-4 years**. It is sown both as an annual and perennial crop. The crop is generally grown in irrigated areas to dry tracts and yields best in well-drained sandy loam soils.

The best time for sowing [વાવણી] is between **early October to the end of November**. The first cutting is ready after **2-2.5 months** of sowing [વાવણી]. During the rainy season, its growth is affected by other monsoon grasses. After the rains, when the soil dries up, it is harvested; otherwise, there is a risk of roots being pulled out during harvesting [કાપણી/લણણી]. If grown as a perennial crop, it may yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ] **1000-1200 quintals per hectare**; when taken as an annual (up to June), the yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ] is **700-900 quintals per hectare**.

## Hybrid Napier [હાઈબ્રિડ નેપિયર] Bajra [બાજરી] Grass

Hybrid Napier [હાઈબ્રિડ નેપિયર] grass is a tall, fast-growing, year-round fodder grass [ઘાસ] cultivated in subtropical climates. It is nutritious, succulent, and palatable. The fodder contains 10% protein [પ્રોટીન]. It responds well to nitrogen fertilizers and organic manure. Bright sunshine with light rainfall is highly favorable for the crop.
## Agricultural Practices
- Light loamy and sandy soils are preferred over heavy soils. Deep soils rich in organic matter yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ] the best results.
- Requires deep, weed-free, and well-pulverized soil; ideal after 3-4 ploughings followed by leveling.
- The crop does not perform well in flood [પૂર]-prone or waterlogged areas.

- In rainfed regions, planting is done at the onset of the monsoon, while in irrigated areas, it can be done at any time of the year. Propagation is done using root or stem cuttings. Medium-aged stem cuttings from the lower two-thirds of the plant sprout faster than older ones.
- Root or stem cuttings with two nodes should be planted at a 45° angle, 5 cm deep, with the lower end downward, ensuring one node is below the soil and the other above the surface.
- For pure hybrid Napier [હાઈબ્રિડ નેપિયર] grass, a spacing of 100x50 cm (100 cm between rows and 50 cm between plants) is recommended.

- Apply 15 tonnes of farmyard manure, 50 kg nitrogen, 50 kg phosphorus [ફોસ્ફરસ], and 40 kg potash per hectare at sowing [વાવણી], and 50 kg nitrogen per hectare after each harvest. Repeat this annually.
- In acidic soils, apply lime at 500 kg per hectare every two years.
- Irrigate immediately after planting and subsequently as needed.
- Keep the field weed-free by manual weeding (using a khurpi or hoe) during the first two months. Control wild grasses and other weeds by hand during the onset of winter in November.
- The first harvest should be done 75 days after planting, and subsequent harvests at 45-60 day intervals, cutting 10-15 cm above ground level.

## What is Silage?
Silage refers to fodder preserved through fermentation [આથવણ] in an airtight environment [પર્યાવરણ] for an extended period. In simple terms, silage is pickled green fodder [લીલો ચારો].
## Rules for Making Silage:

1. Silage can be made during the rainy season when green fodder [લીલો ચારો] is abundant and drying is not feasible, to preserve the fodder. Even if excess green fodder [લીલો ચારો] remains after feeding animals, it can be preserved as silage.
2. Since crops for silage are harvested early, other crops can also be cultivated, allowing more livestock [પશુઓ] to be maintained per acre.
3. If green fodder [લીલો ચારો] has matured due to special circumstances, making silage is preferable to drying, as animals consume it readily.

4. Green fodder [લીલો ચારો] can be stored in the form of silage for a long time and used during shortages, providing high-quality green fodder [લીલો ચારો] to animals at a low cost throughout the year.
5. Making silage preserves nutrients like carotene (Vitamin A) better than dry fodder [સુકો ચારો].
6. Animals prefer silage. The digestibility [પાચનશક્તિ] of fodder increases when made into silage.
7. Dry fodder [સુકો ચારો] requires more storage space, whereas the same quantity of silage requires less space.
8. There is a risk of fire accidents during the storage of dry fodder [સુકો ચારો], whereas no such risk exists in silage storage.

9. Silage can also be prepared from commonly unused green fodder [લીલો ચારો] such as *kunwadiya* (weeds), sugarcane tops, *jhanzvo* (grass species), *dhaman* (Cenchrus ciliaris), *shaniyar* (sorghum [જુવાર] stubble), etc.
10. In areas without irrigation [પિયત] facilities, silage fulfills the need for green fodder [લીલો ચારો].

1. Type of Silo – Surface silos are best due to ease of ensiling.
2. Dry Matter [સૂકો પદાર્થ] of fodder – Ideal 30-35 percent.

5. Sealing [સીલ કરવું] of silo – To prevent inflow of air and water into the silo.

# Silage (Preservation [જાળવણી] of Green Fodder [લીલો ચારો])
## What is Silage?

Silage is a method of preserving green fodder [લીલો ચારો] in a succulent state when its nutrient content is high, allowing it to be stored for extended periods. Similar to how grains are used in animal [પશુ] feed [ચારો] during scarcity or when fresh fodder is unavailable, silage serves as a preserved form of green fodder [લીલો ચારો] for livestock [પશુઓ].
## Silage Preparation Process:

- Silage should be prepared when green fodder [લીલો ચારો] is abundant during the rainy season and cannot be fully utilized immediately, or when fodder growth continues even after meeting the livestock [પશુઓ]'s immediate needs.

- The optimal time for silage preparation is when the crop is at the right maturity stage for harvesting [કાપણી/લણણી]. This ensures that during the year, the same land can produce additional fodder to sustain livestock [પશુઓ].

- Harvesting [કાપણી/લણણી] green fodder [લીલો ચારો] at its peak nutrient content and converting it into silage ensures livestock [પશુઓ] receive high-quality feed [ચારો]. Without proper silage knowledge [જ્ઞાન/માહિતી], one might resort to using overripe or mature fodder, which has lower nutrient content and fails to maintain animal [પશુ] health.
- It is essential to chop the fodder into small pieces using a chopper to facilitate proper packing.
- Green fodder [લીલો ચારો] should be cut, chopped (chopped into small pieces), and packed daily in layers. After packing, it should be sealed daily to prevent air exposure.

- Silage allows green fodder [લીલો ચારો] to be stored for extended periods, ensuring its use during fodder scarcity and providing high-quality green fodder [લીલો ચારો] to livestock [પશુઓ] throughout the year.
- Nutrients like carotene (Vitamin A), which are lost in dry fodder [સુકો ચારો], and other nutrients that degrade during drying, are preserved in higher quantities due to silage preparation.
- Silage preparation enhances the digestibility [પાચનશક્તિ] and palatability [સ્વાદિષ્ટતા] of fodder.
- Silage requires less storage space compared to dry fodder [સુકો ચારો].
- Dry fodder [સુકો ચારો] storage carries a risk of accidental fires, whereas silage storage does not.

- In areas with limited grazing land [ચરિયાણ] or during droughts, purchasing green fodder [લીલો ચારો] can be expensive. Preparing silage ensures a year-round supply of green fodder [લીલો ચારો]. (For example, 15 kg of good-quality silage can replace 3 kg of dry fodder [સુકો ચારો].)
## Important Considerations for Silage Feeding:
> Silage should be **opened and fed after 45–50 days**. Start with **5–10 kg** per animal [પશુ] and gradually increase to **20 kg per day** as needed.
> For animals **under 1 year**, feed [ચારો] **8–10 kg**, and for those **above 1 year**, feed [ચારો] **10–20 kg** based on requirement.
> Avoid feeding silage immediately after milking [દોહવું] to prevent **off-flavors in milk**.
> Mixing [મિશ્રણ કરવું] silage with dry fodder [સુકો ચારો] improves **digestibility [પાચનશક્તિ]** and reduces **bloat [ગેસ આફરો,ફૂલી જવું,] risk**.
> Do **not** feed [ચારો] silage from **moldy or spoiled sections** (especially near walls) to prevent health issues.

## **Introduction:**

For optimal growth, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન], and reproductive functions in dairy animals, the body [બૈડા/બરડા] requires certain essential elements that can be adequately supplied through high-quality feed [ચારો] and supplements. However, if these minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો] are either deficient in the soil or present in inadequate quantities, their absorption in the digestive system may also be insufficient. Consequently, to meet the body [બૈડા/બરડા]’s requirements, livestock [પશુઓ] must be provided with targeted mineral supplements to compensate for the lack of natural mineral uptake. Generally, mineral mixtures play a crucial role in fulfilling the daily mineral needs of animals.
- **What is a Mineral Mixture [મિશ્રણ ખનીજ તત્વો]?**

A mineral mixture [મિશ્રણ ખનીજ તત્વો] is a blend of essential minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો] required by the animal [પશુ]’s body [બૈડા/બરડા], provided in appropriate proportions. In dairy animals such as cows and buffaloes, minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો] play a vital role in regulating internal physiological processes. They are essential for the animal [પશુ]’s growth, productivity [ઉત્પાદકતા], and reproductive functions.
- **Why is a Mineral Mixture [મિશ્રણ ખનીજ તત્વો] Necessary in Livestock [પશુઓ]?**
Mineral mixtures are necessary in livestock [પશુઓ] for the following reasons:
1. **Enhances milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન]** in dairy animals.
2. **Improves reproductive efficiency [કાર્યક્ષમતા]** in both males and females.
3. **Reduces the duration of calving [વિયાણ] intervals.**
4. **Aids in the growth of calves (male/female).**
5. **Improves digestibility [પાચનશક્તિ] of consumed feed [ચારો].**
6. **Boosts disease resistance** in animals.
7. **Ensures the birth of healthy calves.**
8. **Increases the productive lifespan of livestock [પશુઓ].**

9. **Prevents reproductive disorders** such as **retained placenta [માટી ન ખસવી], dystocia [વિયાણમાં મુશ્કેલી], prolapse [દેહ બતાવવી/આર બતાવવું (ગર્ભાશય બહાર આવવું)], and conditions like ketosis [કિટોસીસ/ઊર્જાની કમીથી થતો રોગ].**

Typically, for dairy cows and buffaloes to produce milk daily, they should be fed 1 kg of balanced concentrate [દાણ], 4 kg of green leguminous fodder, 8 kg of green cereal fodder, or 6 to 6 kg of dry fodder [સુકો ચારો] or straw [કડબ/ભૂસું], husk, etc., as available and preferred. To enhance milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન], cows should be given 500 grams of high-energy concentrate [દાણ] per kilogram of milk produced. For buffaloes, 600 grams of high-energy concentrate [દાણ] should be provided per kilogram of milk. For crossbred cows producing up to 10 liters or more of milk, a balanced diet should include at least 18% protein [પ્રોટીન] and 68 to 70% total digestible nutrients (TDN).
## Importance of Mineral Elements

Mineral elements hold significant importance in animal [પશુ] feed [ચારો] because they are essential for body [બૈડા/બરડા] structure and various physiological functions. Moreover, animals cannot synthesize minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો] on their own, so these must be supplied through their diet. Mineral requirements can be categorized based on the body [બૈડા/બરડા]'s needs:

1. **Macrominerals (Major Minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો]):** These are required in larger quantities in the body [બૈડા/બરડા], such as Calcium [કેલ્શિયમ], Phosphorus [ફોસ્ફરસ], Sodium, Chlorine, Potassium, and Sulfur.
2. **Microminerals (Trace Minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો]):** These are required in smaller quantities, such as Iron, Copper, Zinc, Manganese, Cobalt, Chromium, and Selenium.

This disease commonly occurs in high-yielding dairy animals one month after calving [વિયાણ]. Maintaining blood sugar levels is crucial for energy regulation [નિયમન] in the body [બૈડા/બરડા].

When there is an imbalance between the body [બૈડા/બરડા]'s energy requirements for milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] and its availability, blood sugar levels drop. As a result, the body [બૈડા/બરડા] burns stored fat [ફેટ], producing ketone bodies as a byproduct.
# Signs of Ketosis [કિટોસીસ/ઊર્જાની કમીથી થતો રોગ]
In high-yielding dairy animals, milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] decreases after 1 month post-calving [વિયાણ પછી].
- The animal [પશુ] consumes dry fodder [સુકો ચારો] properly but reduces intake of green fodder [લીલો ચારો] and eventually stops eating concentrate [દાણ] feed [ચારો].
- Subcutaneous fat [ફેટ] decreases, making the animal [પશુ] appear emaciated.
- A distinct sweet odor is noticed in the breath; in some cases, this sweet odor may also be present in urine, mouth, and milk.
- In advanced stages, the animal [પશુ] may walk in circles, hold its head high, and behave as if blind.
# Preventive Measures for Ketosis [કિટોસીસ/ઊર્જાની કમીથી થતો રોગ]

Do not keep the animal [પશુ] hungry, nor overfeed it.
## Gradually Increase Concentrate [દાણ] After Calving [વિયાણ]
Generally, feed [ચારો] slightly more than the animal [પશુ]'s milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] capacity.

A little girl held an apple in each hand. Her mother, smiling affectionately, asked her in a loving tone:
*""Sweetheart, you have two apples—will you give one to Mommy?""*

*""Mommy, take this apple. It’s sweeter.""*
