- Lumpy Skin Disease [ગાંઠિયો રોગ] (LSD) is a viral disease [વિષાણુથી થતો રોગ] affecting cattle [પશુ] and buffalo [ભેંસ], causing nodules on the skin and other parts of the body [બૈડા/બરડા].
- This disease is caused by a poxvirus, leading to small to large nodules appearing on the animal [પશુ]'s skin and other body [બૈડા/બરડા] parts.
- Due to this disease, other animals in contact with the infected animal [પશુ] can also become affected.
## Transmission:
- The primary mode of transmission of this disease is through insect vectors such as flies, mosquitoes, and ticks [ઇતરડી].
- Secretions from infected animals, such as blood, nasal discharge, saliva, etc., aid in the spread of the disease.
## Symptoms of the Disease:
- High fever [તાવ] (103-104°F).
- Discharge from the eyes and nose.
- Reduced feed [ચારો] intake.
- Decrease in milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન].
- General lethargy and depression in the surrounding environment [પર્યાવરણ].
- Hard nodules appear on the skin of the animal [પશુ]'s body [બૈડા/બરડા], which can be 2 to 5 cm thick. These nodules are round and firm.
- Swelling on the legs and hooves can lead to lameness [લંગડાપણું].
- Abortion [પશુ તરવાઈ જવું] may occur in pregnant [ગાભણ] animals.
- Infected animals may become infertile.
## Control and Prevention:
- Prevent the movement of animals from disease-affected areas.
- Isolate sick animals to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy animals.
- Keep healthy animals away from sick animals.
- Apply antiseptic ointments on wounds and ensure that flies and other insects do not come into contact with the wounds.
- Disinfectants such as Domoline (2%), Dinol (2% for 15 minutes), Sodium Hypochlorite (2-3%), and Quaternary Ammonium Compounds (0.5%) can be used for controlling the spread of the disease.

Infected animals often recover on their own within **2 to 3 weeks**, but the disease causes economic losses due to reduced milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન]. While the mortality [મૃત્યુદર] rate is low, the high infection [ચેપ] rate makes prevention crucial.
→ **Symptoms of the Disease**
- Fever [તાવ] lasting **2 to 3 days**.
- Hard, round lumps (**2 to 5 cm in diameter**) appear on the animal [પશુ]’s body [બૈડા/બરડા], penetrating deep into the skin and sometimes the muscles.

# Sex-Sorted Semen

Artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (AI) conventionally uses unsorted semen doses. In the field of artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન], recent advancements enable the use of **sex-sorted semen** to strategically enhance livestock [પશુઓ] farming. While conventional semen insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] results in a male-to-female calf [પાડુ/વાછરડું] ratio of approximately **51:48**, sex-sorted semen increases the probability of female calves to **80%**. This reduces the surplus of unwanted male calves and optimizes resource allocation per animal [પશુ], thereby increasing the female livestock [પશુઓ] population.
## Guidelines for Using Sex-Sorted Semen
- The inseminator must be certified or trained in performing insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન].
- Sex-sorted semen should preferably be used on **heifers/young cows** of optimal age.
- It is advisable to use sex-sorted semen primarily for **first insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]** rather than repeat inseminations in animals.
- The animal [પશુ] should exhibit **regular estrous cycles (18–21 days)**.
- The animal [પશુ] must be provided with **regular mineral mixtures, deworming [કૃમિનાશક દવા] treatments, and balanced feed [ચારો]** for optimal reproductive health.
- The **Body Condition Score [શારીરિક અવસ્થાના ગુણાંક] (BCS)** of the animal [પશુ] should be between **2.5 and 3.5**; animals with lower scores are unsuitable for insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન].
- The **uterine condition** of the animal [પશુ] must be healthy, with no signs of infections or abnormalities. Animals with a history of repeated abortions should not be used.

- The insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] cost, as determined by the **AI association**, will be separate from the technician’s fee. The current price of a sex-sorted semen dose [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] is **₹50/-**.

### (b) Irregular Estrus Cycle (Rutukāṇ/Ṛtuchakra):
The estrous cycle in animals can be classified as:
- **Short (6-12 days)**
- **Normal (12-24 days)**
- **Long (24-41 days)**
Similarly, the duration of the estrous cycle may vary:
- **Very short (≤8 days)**
- **Short (8-12 days)**
- **Moderately short (12-18 days)**
- **Normal (18-24 days)**
- **Long (≥25 days)**
Animals with **short or long estrous cycles** (excluding normal cycles) may require veterinary consultation to induce estrus, as such irregularities can indicate underlying reproductive disorders.

## **Key Considerations for Farmers**
1. **Timing of Heat Detection [વેતરની ઓળખ]**
- Buffaloes typically exhibit heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] signs **around sunrise and sunset**. Most buffaloes come into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] in the **evening**.
- Farmers should **observe each animal [પશુ]’s reproductive organs closely during early morning and late evening**, especially when buffaloes are kept in shaded areas.
- If a buffalo [ભેંસ] shows heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] signs in the evening, **insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] should be planned for the next morning** for better conception [ગર્ભધારણ] rates.
2. **Maintain a Breeding [પ્રજનન] Record**
- Farmers should **maintain a register** recording details such as:
- Date of last heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું]
- Date of last calving [વિયાણ]
- Date of last insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન]
- Milk yield [ઉતારો/પેદાશ] data

- This record helps predict the **expected heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] date**, allowing farmers to **closely monitor buffaloes between 2 PM and 3 PM** for signs of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું].

- After calving [વિયાણ], the **uterus [ગર્ભાશય] takes about 45–50 days to return to its normal condition**. Farmers should **start monitoring [દેખરેખ/નિરીક્ષણ] buffaloes for heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] between 60–80 days post-calving [વિયાણ પછી]** to ensure timely breeding [પ્રજનન].
3. **Provide Adequate Shade**
- Buffaloes should be **kept in well-ventilated, shaded areas** to prevent heat stress [ગરમીનો તણાવ], which can suppress heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] signs.
4. **Manage Environmental Conditions**
- **High temperatures can reduce heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] signs**, so farmers should **prevent direct sunlight exposure** by providing **shade under trees or shelters**.
- Efforts should be made to **maintain a cool and comfortable environment [પર્યાવરણ]** for buffaloes to improve heat detection [વેતરની ઓળખ].
After tying the animal [પશુ] in the shed, spraying water on its body [બૈડા/બરડા] using sprinklers can lower the body temperature [શરીરનું તાપમાન] as well as the ambient temperature.

In high-milk-producing animals prone to anestrus [વિયાણ પછી ગરમીમાં ન આવવું], it is essential to follow scientific recommendations to adjust milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] schedules. This condition is observed, particularly in cases of inadequate and imbalanced nutrition [પોષણ] or certain genetic disorders, where seasonal anestrus [વિયાણ પછી ગરમીમાં ન આવવું] (absence of estrus) delays the onset of puberty [તરુણાવસ્થા/પુખ્તતા] in heifers and leads to infertility [વંધ્યત્વ] in cows due to the lack of estrous cycles. Such conditions may also occur post-partum, primarily due to imbalanced nutrition [પોષણ], deficiencies in vitamins [વિટામિન્સ] or minerals [ખનીજ તત્વો], insufficient availability of certain endogenous secretions, and declining body weight [શરીરનું વજન] caused by high milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] in animals. Post-partum complications such as **pyometra** (pus accumulation in the uterus [ગર્ભાશય]), ovarian inflammation, **mastitis [આઉનો/બાવલાનો સોજો]**, and **ketosis [કિટોસીસ/ઊર્જાની કમીથી થતો રોગ]** can also render animals anestrus [વિયાણ પછી ગરમીમાં ન આવવું] and infertile.

In older animals, worn-out or lost teeth weaken digestive efficiency [કાર્યક્ષમતા], preventing them from consuming or digesting adequate nutrition [પોષણ]. Such animals lose weight and suffer from anestrus [વિયાણ પછી ગરમીમાં ન આવવું].

Additionally, chronic physical ailments like **tuberculosis**, **actinomycosis**, **fascioliasis**, and infestations by external parasites such as intestinal worms [પેટમાં કીડા કરમિયા], lice, ticks [ઇતરડી], and mites cause weight loss [વજનમાં ઘટાડો] and lead to anestrus [વિયાણ પછી ગરમીમાં ન આવવું].

In cases of **silent heat [શાંત વેતર]**, cows do not exhibit estrous signs primarily due to insufficient estrogen secretion. Nutritional imbalances, environmental factors (temperature, humidity, sunlight), and animal [પશુ] management play a crucial role.
Temporary infertility [વંધ્યત્વ] can be due to the following reasons:
1. **Animal [પશુ] not coming into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] (estrus)**
- Lack of nutritional planning
- Presence of **Persistent Corpus Luteum (PCL)**
- Underdeveloped ovaries
- Errors in detecting heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] signs
2. **Animal [પશુ] coming into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] but not conceiving**
- Inadequate nutrition [પોષણ] (most likely cause)
- Hormonal imbalances
- Infectious diseases of the uterus [ગર્ભાશય] (high likelihood)
### Measures for Preventing Infertility [વંધ્યત્વ]
- Provide calves/heifers with a regular and balanced amount of mineral mixture [મિશ્રણ ખનીજ તત્વો], calf starter [બચ્ચા દાણ], and balanced feed [ચારો].
- Along with proper medical treatment, ensure a nutritious diet and adequate use of mineral mixtures.
- Deworm the animals and accurately detect signs of silent heat [શાંત વેતર] in animals that come into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું].
- Timely perform artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] (12 to 18 hours) for animals in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું].
- For animals in extreme heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], perform a second artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] after 24 hours.
- If an animal [પશુ] does not conceive after three inseminations, avoid further inseminations and seek diagnosis [નિદાન] and treatment.
- Ensure that the artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] process is carried out with complete hygiene and precautions.
- If any abnormalities are noticed in an animal [પશુ] in heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], conduct proper examination and treatment.
- Regularly check every 19-21 days post-artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] to see if the animal [પશુ] comes back into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું].
- Conduct pregnancy diagnosis [ખાલી ગાભણ તપાસ] 75 to 90 days after artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન].
- Provide appropriate treatment for complications related to retained placenta [માટી ન ખસવી] and metritis [ગર્ભાશયની દીવાલ નો સોજો] during parturition.
- Ensure that the animal [પશુ] is ready for artificial insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] within 60 to 90 days post-parturition with proper nutritional planning.
- Dry off the animal [પશુ] in the last two months of pregnancy [ગર્ભ] and provide a balanced diet.
- Avoid unnecessary use of cooling injections in pregnant [ગાભણ] animals.
- Isolate animals that have aborted.

After calving [વિયાણ], the cow [ગાય]/buffalo [ભેંસ] licks the calf [પાડુ/વાછરડું] to clean it. The placenta [મેલી/જર] (afterbirth) usually detaches within **6 to 8 hours** post-delivery. However, if it does not expel within **12 hours in summer** or **18 to 24 hours in winter**, a veterinarian should intervene to remove it. The expelled placenta [મેલી/જર] should be promptly disposed of to prevent the animal [પશુ] from consuming it. The freshly calved cow [ગાય]’s hindquarters, tail, vulva, udder [બાવલું], and teats should be washed with lukewarm water and dried. The newborn calf [પાડુ/વાછરડું] should then be fed **colostrum [ખીરૂ]** (first milk) either directly from the udder [બાવલું] or by milking [દોહવું] it into a container.

The cow [ગાય] should be given warm water to drink as much as it can. Since calving [વિયાણ] is an extremely strenuous process, much of the animal [પશુ]’s energy is expended. Therefore, a **calving [વિયાણ] ration (Vichardaan)**—a nutrient-rich, energy-boosting feed [ચારો]—should be provided. The calving [વિયાણ] ration typically includes:
- **1 kg wheat bran [ઘઉંનું થૂલું]**
- **500 g jaggery [ગોળ]**
- **1 kg boiled millet (bajra [બાજરી])**
- **100 g fennel seeds (suva)**
- **100 g fenugreek [મેથી] (methi)**
- **100 g dry ginger [સૂંઠ] (sunth)**
- **100 g asafoetida [હીંગ] (asaliyo)**
For the first **10 to 15 days post-calving [વિયાણ પછી]**, the calving [વિયાણ] ration should be gradually reduced while increasing other feed [ચારો]. Feeding the calving [વિયાણ] ration helps:
- Restore the cow [ગાય]’s energy,
- Aid in uterine recovery [સાજા થવું], and
- Boost milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન].

Routine vaccination [રસીકરણ] of the susceptible population (including sheep, goats, and pigs) within a 5 km radius of the farm and in villages from which frequent purchases are planned (e.g., villages in progeny testing [સંતતિ પરીક્ષણ] programs) is recommended.

As a result of Banas Dairy’s Farm Consultancy Service and Progressive Milk Producer Development Program, around 150 milk producers in Jalla have adopted a scientific approach and constructed open sheds, which have proven to be a boon in animal husbandry [પશુપાલન]. According to their feedback, the benefits of open sheds are as follows:

1. Relief from the task of removing dung. Today’s younger generation feels embarrassed about handling dung, but with open sheds and a scientific approach to animal husbandry [પશુપાલન], young people are now encouraged to engage in modern animal husbandry [પશુપાલન].
2. Animals kept in open sheds have a negligible incidence of disease and remain healthy.
3. Keeping animals in open sheds increases milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] by 500 grams to 1 liter per animal [પશુ] per day.
4. There is a notable increase in fat [ફેટ] and SNF [એસ.એન.એફ.] (Solid Not Fat [ફેટ]) content in the milk.
5. The problem of animals returning to heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] is largely resolved.
6. Tied animals are more prone to tympany (bloat [ગેસ આફરો,ફૂલી જવું,]), but this disease does not occur in animals kept in open sheds.
7. Animals in open sheds do not suffer from intestinal issues as tied animals do.

8. The manure produced from dung and urine in open sheds has a higher nitrogen content. This manure needs to be used only half as much as regular dung manure, and its effect on crops is even better than chemical fertilizers.
9. Animals tied in sheds tend to become restless due to heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], but when left in open sheds, they stop showing such restlessness [બેચેની].
10. Keeping animals in open sheds reduces labor costs, thereby decreasing the overall cost of milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન].
Thus, with the above benefits observed by farmers keeping animals in open sheds, it is strongly recommended that all farmers in Jalla construct open sheds for their livestock [પશુઓ].

**1. Direct Physical Damage**
*   **Blood Loss & Weakness:** They suck blood, which leads to anemia and general weakness. For example, 100 ticks on a 400kg animal can suck approximately 1 liter of blood per day.
*   **Skin Issues:** They cause constant itching, skin irritation, rashes, lesions, and hair loss. Some cause specific skin diseases like mange (scabies).
*   **Toxicity:** Certain parasites, like ticks, release toxins that can lead to ""tick paralysis.""
**2. Disease Transmission**
They act as vectors for serious hemoprotozoan and other diseases, including:
*   **Theileriosis:** Causes high fever, anemia, and swollen lymph nodes.
*   **Babesiosis:** Known as redwater disease (hemoglobinuria).
*   **Anaplasmosis:** Causes high fever and anemia.
*   **Trypanosomiasis:** Commonly observed in buffaloes.
**3. Impact on Productivity & Growth**
*   **Milk & Weight Loss:** There is a permanent reduction in milk production capacity and significant weight loss (e.g., an animal with 40 ticks can lose 1.5 to 2 kg per month).
*   **Stunted Growth:** In young calves and heifers, growth and development are stunted, and their immune systems are weakened.
*   **Behavioral Changes:** Animals become irritable, restless, and may reduce their intake of fodder and water.
**4. Economic Impact**

In India, ticks and similar parasites cause an estimated annual loss of ₹3,151 crores in the livestock sector.","External parasites, such as ticks, lice, and mites, can cause a variety of problems for cattle and buffalo. **૧. સીધું શારીરિક નુકસાન**
*   **રક્તની ઉણપ અને નબળાઈ:** તેઓ લોહી ચૂસે છે, જેના કારણે એનિમિયા અને સામાન્ય નબળાઈ આવે છે. ઉદાહરણ તરીકે, ૪૦૦ કિલોના પ્રાણી પર ૧૦૦ ટિક દરરોજ આશરે ૧ લિટર લોહી ચૂસી શકે છે.
*   **ત્વચાની સમસ્યાઓ:** તેઓ સતત ખંજવાળ, ત્વચામાં બળતરા, ફોલ્લીઓ, ચાંદા અને વાળ ખરવાનું કારણ બને છે. કેટલાક ચોક્કસ ત્વચા રોગો જેમ કે ખંજવાળ (સ્કેબીઝ)નું કારણ બને છે.

*   **થિલરીયોસિસ:** આ રોગથી તીવ્ર તાવ, એનિમિયા અને લસિકા ગાંઠોમાં સોજો આવે છે.
*   **બેબેસિયોસિસ:** આને લાલ પાણીનો રોગ (હેમોગ્લોબિનુરિયા) તરીકે ઓળખવામાં આવે છે.

*   **ટ્રાયપેનોસોમિયાસિસ:** આ રોગ સામાન્ય રીતે ભેંસોમાં જોવા મળે છે.

*   **દૂધ અને વજનમાં ઘટાડો:** દૂધ ઉત્પાદનની ક્ષમતામાં કાયમી ઘટાડો થાય છે અને નોંધપાત્ર વજનમાં ઘટાડો થાય છે (ઉદાહરણ તરીકે, ૪૦ ટિક ધરાવતું પ્રાણી દર મહિને ૧.૫ થી ૨ કિલો વજન ગુમાવી શકે છે).
*   **વૃદ્ધિમાં અવરોધ:** યુવાન વાછરડાં અને બકરીઓમાં, વૃદ્ધિ અને વિકાસમાં અવરોધ આવે છે અને તેમની રોગપ્રતિકારક શક્તિ નબળી પડે છે.

If heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] persists in the following morning, another AI may be required on the same evening.
- If the animal [પશુ] does not become pregnant [ગાભણ], it will come into heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું] after 18-21 days.
- After 21 days of insemination [કૃત્રિમ બીજદાન] the animal [પશુ] should be observed for symptoms of heat [ગરમીમાં આવવું, વેતરમો આવવું], especially during early morning and late evening hours.

- During last few days of the dry period [વસૂકેલો ગાળો], watch the cow [ગાય] closely for signs of calving [વિયાણ]. Ensure safe delivery in a calving [વિયાણ] pen. ## Maintenance of Dairy Records

Maintenance of proper records helps in efficient management of a dairy farm. Record keeping [રેકોર્ડ રાખવો] is essential for evaluation of the performance and for taking corrective measures so as to maximize profits. Application of computer has very crucial role in dairy farm record management.
The following records should be maintained at a dairy farm:
i) Date of birth and pedigree [વંશાવલી] information (at least parents and preferably grandparents) of the animals.
ii) Records on growth.
iii) Reproduction [પ્રજનન] records (oestrus, breeding [પ્રજનન], pregnancy diagnosis [ખાલી ગાભણ તપાસ] and calving [વિયાણ]).
iv) Milk production [દૂધ ઉત્પાદન] records (daily).
v) Health and veterinary record (vaccination [રસીકરણ]/ drenching with anthelmintics, dusting/spraying/ dipping for the prevention of parasites).
vi) Treatment of diseases and disorders.
vii) Feeding item records (daily consumption of green fodder [લીલો ચારો], straw [કડબ/ભૂસું] and concentrates) estimated values.
viii) Periodic test of milk fat [ફેટ], SNF [એસ.એન.એફ.] and other quality parameters such as bacterial counts, antibiotic and pesticide [જીવાણુ નાશક] residues.

Besides above records, complete farm business records (purchase of feed [ચારો], seed, fodder, fertilizers, veterinary medicines, irrigation [પિયત], implements, electricity and fuel expenses, sale of milk, animals, skin, manure, labour wages etc.) should also be maintained.
